newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs end off, trade slows ahead of Carnival.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs end off, trade slows ahead of Carnival.

text.p: Brazilian stocks posted small losses at Thursday's close, weighed down by a volatile Dow Industrials, in weaker trade ahead of next week's Carnival holiday, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 49 most active shares closed off 0.29 percent at 81,479 points. Volume was a moderate 456.4 million reais ($438.8 million).
"We had expected a firm market today, but volatility on Wall Street helped to break our expectations," a senior trader said.
Analysts said the selling pressure could also be attributed to speculation ahead of Feb 17 options expiry.
Today's market was also affected by the fact that one of the top blue-chips was not traded. Brazilian bolsas halted request by Brazil's Securities and Exchange Commission (CVM).
The CVM requested the suspension until the company provides explanation on a Rio court sentence ordering it to pay more than three billion reais to Petroquisa's minority shareholders.
Petroquisa is Petrobras' holding company in the petrochemical sector and most of its subsidiaries were sold off in the first phase of Brazil's privatization program.
Petrobras was expected to issue a statement on the court order today but so far the company has made no comment on the matter.
Preferred shares of Petroquisa rose 80 percent to 63 reais.
Bellwether Telebras closed off 0.76 percent at 92 reais.

State mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce preferred dropped 2.54 percent to 24.95 reais. Traders were disappointed that bid specifications for the company's selloff will only be available in late February or early March.
